terms.comment: A legal maxim in this shape. The rule is in Justinian’s Code (below); the Decretals of Gregory IX give it as quī prior est tempore, jūre potior esse vidētur. We have found no ancient source for Traupman’s wording.

evidence: Cod. Just. 8.17.2: nam cum dē pignore utraque pars contendat, praevalet jūre, quī praevenit tempore
terms.comment: Literally “he who comes first in time prevails in law”: an imperial ruling on two claims to the same pledge.

sources: John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, cited by printed page; each phrase checked against the searchable text of the book.
